claimBoundary: Self-run mapping of MELRA against the AARM v1.0 minimum tests, using cases written by the MELRA project. Not AARM conformance, not an "AARM-compliant" claim, and not reviewed by the AARM Technical Working Group or the CSA. AARM publishes no test IDs or harness. The IDs (R1-T1..R9-T1, in page order), the case design and the pass criteria are MELRA's own reading of the spec.

paper.attribution: Errico, H. (2026). Autonomous Action Runtime Management (AARM): A System Specification for Securing AI-Driven Actions at Runtime. arXiv:2602.09433v1

conformancePage.tableText: The minimum-tests table, the page's second table: each row's cell texts trimmed and joined with " | ", rows joined with "\n", header row included (22 rows), UTF-8. Only this hash is kept, never the text.

siteSource.license: no LICENSE file at this commit

counting.case: not_implemented when a needed interface is missing or its steps are not written yet (counts as fail); pass when every assertion passes; fail when an effect assertion fails or none passes; partial otherwise
counting.test: pass when every case passes; fail when any case fails an effect assertion or no case is pass or partial; partial otherwise. An environment skip is never a pass. n/a only from this manifest, only for a SHOULD, with a written reason

deviations.site: a denial after a step-up timeout is required
receipts for all five decisions, modify included
proprietary-only formats do not satisfy it
deviations.paper: OCSF, CEF or a documented custom format (VII-C2)

deviations.site: listed under R2 and marked SHOULD
organisational conditions for a conformance claim

tests.test: An action that a deny rule matches must not run, and the denial must leave a receipt.
An action that meets a defer condition is suspended with no effect, and a deferral receipt is written.
With the governing system unavailable, a submitted action fails rather than running ungoverned.
Across a sequence of actions, the policy engine at step N is given every earlier action and the data classifications they involved.
Where prior context is hash-chained, altering an earlier entry is detected.

tests.requirement: R3 Policy evaluation with intent alignment
tests.test: A forbidden action is denied at once, whatever context surrounds it.

generatedFrom.rule: r3t1.<context>.<GovBench id>, for every GovBench case with one of the prefixes that expects a refusal; allowlist only for programs MELRA always denies; enforced skips cases whose policy turns every guardrail off (R1-T3 covers that)

tests.requirement: R3 Policy evaluation with intent alignment
tests.test: An otherwise allowed action that follows access to sensitive data is denied because of that context.

tests.requirement: R3 Policy evaluation with intent alignment
tests.test: An otherwise denied action accompanied by confirming context results in step-up or allow.

tests.requirement: R3 Policy evaluation with intent alignment
tests.test: An action whose context is ambiguous or contradictory is deferred.
Each of the five decisions behaves as named: allow runs, deny blocks, modify transforms, step-up pauses, defer suspends.
A step-up that gets no answer before its timeout ends as a denial.
A deferral that is not resolved before its timeout ends as a denial.
Receipts for all five decisions carry the requester's context, the delegation chain and the policy version or hash, as the receipt schema requires.
A receipt's signature can be checked offline, and it holds.
Changing the requester context or the policy hash in a receipt makes its signature check fail.
A deferred action's receipt records why it was deferred, how it was resolved and when.
Actions from different principals and sessions leave receipts that attribute each to the right identity, with its role or privilege scope.
When a deferred action is resolved, the resolution receipt keeps the original requester's identity.
An action sequence that drifts past a threshold triggers an alert, a deferral or an escalation.
tests.na: MELRA's decision path may not call a model or depend on model output, and the drift metric this test names needs an embedding model. Section VII lets a SHOULD be omitted with a written justification. The deterministic proxy listed under informational is reported and never counted.

tests.test: With export to a SIEM configured, events arrive in the expected schema, deferrals included.
A credential issued for a read operation cannot be used to write.
